column1: # Targeted verdict queue — one request per line:
#   <40-char sha>
# The watcher drains these FIRST among its idle phases. A request is satisfied
# when that sha has a verdict at that tier, so lines need no deletion and a
# repeat is a no-op. Stale lines cost one archive lookup per cycle; tidy at
# will, but nothing breaks if you never do.
# STRUCK 2026-08-28 by frank-coordinator, unserved: the ab51855df full request.
# It asked for the pin COMMIT; the question was about the pin TREE 83468c5462d4,
# which verify_pin answered on its own at 2026-08-27T23:25:33Z (RED, 0 new).
# The request was never read — the resident daemon predated the draining code —
# so serving it now would spend a 3202-job full tier, on the box that is the
# binding constraint, at a sha 20+ testable commits stale, to re-answer an
# answered question. Always --covering first, and check whether an existing
# phase already produces the verdict before queueing.
# STRUCK 2026-08-30 by frankT, unserved: the 440c822e6a80 full request.
# CONTAMINATED, not stale — it is a real sha and it does carry the -O2 promotion,
# but `merge-base --is-ancestor 72b4c47a7 440c822e6a80` is NO, so it carries
# frankB's broken string-literal commit 9588c8535 WITHOUT its revert. A full
# tier there returns RED with the ~24 nilpy jobs frankwasm traced to 9588c8535,
# and those reds land in a row keyed to the promotion — an archive row that
# outlives the session that knows better. Two string-literal-handle changes 36
# minutes apart, one broken, and the target contained both. Naming a SHA when
# the question is about a TREE STATE is the mistake; check what a target
# contains, not only that it exists.
# Replaced by 1d8db8667, verified here to contain 440c822e6 AND 72b4c47a7.
